teams.synopsis: Over 600 points for already — four good WRs and a rising Njoku, with only the Jacobs bye to worry about.
teams.blurb: One of the few people with more than 600 points for, Root's team has multiple superstar talents at every position. The only question mark on this roster is TE, and Njoku is on the rise and could finish the year as a top-7 TE. Jacobs is on a bye this week, so this team will have to look for a replacement, since he has no other RBs on the roster. I'm also intrigued to see what this manager does with his 4 solid WRs, because you can only play 3 per week — that leaves the door open for future trades.

teams.synopsis: Content to sit at 2 for now — the JT addition could reveal this team's real ceiling.
teams.blurb: Staying at 2 this week is exactly what this manager wanted. Staying afloat in the top 4 is all you really need to be set up for playoff success, which is what this manager is looking to achieve. This lineup is looking very dangerous this week with the addition of <mark class="hl-player">JT</mark> — this week will hint at how much success this team can have.

teams.synopsis: Worst team after Week 1, top 5 for three straight weeks since — a healthy Kamara sealed the turnaround.
teams.blurb: I am very happy for this team — after being viewed as one of, if not the, worst teams after Week 1, Malich has found himself in the top 5 three weeks in a row. <mark class="hl-player">Kamara</mark> is officially back, and if <mark class="hl-player">Taysom</mark> hadn't had a career day, this team would've put up even more points. Having the highest PF is not an easy feat this deep into the season, and look for this team to continue winning matchups. This team also has one of the highest projected points for the next couple weeks, which makes continuous fantasy success a real possibility.

teams.synopsis: A quiet week and a rough bye schedule cost the top spot — top-3 upside is still very much alive.
teams.blurb: Brandon takes a fall from being ranked 1st because of the major drop-off in production and the fact that he'll have to win this week with 2 of his top players on bye. I do still think this team is capable of putting up top-3 points, though, and believe this is a reasonable spot for the team — although some managers have called Brandon 'the luckiest manager ever'.

teams.synopsis: A losing record but a playoff lock on talent alone — projected for 120+ this week.
teams.blurb: I'm a huge fan of this team, and even though they have a losing record, I see this team as a lock for the playoffs. The combination of a top WR and a top RB gives this team an exceptionally high ceiling, and I think that will come in handy as they try to get back on track and above .500. Deniz is projected for over 120 points this week, so be ready for this team to stay at the top of these rankings.

teams.synopsis: Henry, Mixon, and Hall make this a championship favorite — if the QB spot ever gets solved.
teams.blurb: I have little doubt that this team can get back to the top of the rankings. The RB trio of <mark class="hl-player">Henry</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Mixon</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Hall</mark> is frightening, and the WRs have the upside to be top-24 every week. This team shouldn't be forgotten about and should be on everyone's radar as a championship favorite. The QB position is the only concern I have with this team, but if he figures that out, he might become unstoppable.

teams.synopsis: The losing streak is over — still unlucky on matchups, but the 2nd-highest PF says wins are coming.
teams.blurb: I knew this team was going to break the losing streak this week, and I think it was well-earned — despite his opponent putting up awful numbers. Aidan no longer has the highest PA, but 2nd-highest is still very unlucky. On the brighter side, this team has the 2nd-highest PF, and for that reason I think this team will continue winning and might creep into the playoff picture by midseason. He takes on Deniz this week, which might be the matchup of the week — either this one or the one between Malich and Ethan.

teams.synopsis: Godwin's comfort and a resurgent Fournette point to consistent 110+ outputs ahead.
teams.blurb: I have Ben at the 8th spot because I feel like this team will start producing consistent 110+ point outputs, with Godwin getting comfortable and Fournette starting to look like his old self. This team still has question marks at TE and flex, but if he figures out how to plug those holes, he'll become an above-average organization.

teams.synopsis: Told to 'leave the league' more than once, yet quietly scoring above the league average all season.
teams.blurb: Jumping up a few spots shouldn't be a surprise to fantasy managers. Charlie has reportedly been told to 'leave the league' multiple times by opposing managers, but his team is 3-2 and has scored more points than the league-average PF — meaning he's been putting up above-average numbers despite the criticism. Also, keep an eye on <mark class="hl-player">Rhamondre Stevenson</mark>; with <mark class="hl-player">Harris</mark> sidelined for multiple weeks, he'll have the backfield all to himself and can be viewed as a mid-tier RB2 at least.

teams.synopsis: Questionable trades and a fading Waddle — Saquon and a returning DHop are the lifeline.
teams.blurb: Oh, how this team has fallen. Recent questionable trades have made me question if this team still has what it takes to make the PFFL playoffs. One nice thing I can say about this team is that <mark class="hl-player">DHop</mark> is coming back soon, which might be the extra support <mark class="hl-player">Waddle</mark> needs. Waddle hasn't looked like himself, and now <mark class="hl-player">Harris</mark> is out for multiple weeks — those things hurt this team, but <mark class="hl-player">Saquon</mark> might be able to make up for the lack of production at RB2. I'd say keep an eye on this team to try and have a bounce-back week.

teams.synopsis: A 3-2 record propped up by injuries — ETN and Zeke need to have huge weeks just to stay afloat.
teams.blurb: I have this team just nudging out Carmine for the 11th spot because of injuries, but if this team continues to put up subpar numbers, it'll drop back down. I know Anthony has a 3-2 record, but how long can it last? His RBs for this week are <mark class="hl-player">ETN</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Zeke</mark> due to a <mark class="hl-player">Pierce</mark> bye week, which makes it very hard to believe this team will win unless his players have season-high outputs. It's also been confirmed that this team wants to trade one of its two WRs to upgrade at RB, but I don't have full confidence that a deal will get done.

teams.synopsis: The league's most unlucky team now — too many questionable spots to trust just yet.
teams.blurb: The TE injury does concern me a little, but then again, it might just be nothing. Carmine made some concerning trades this past week, but I think this team still has the potential to make a playoff run later in the season. This team has the highest PA in the league and has recently surpassed Aidan as the most unlucky team. That being said, I still think a questionable flex, TE, RB2, and QB leave this team as a bottom-5 team for the next couple weeks, at least.

teams.synopsis: The 3rd-lowest PF in the league — trading Kupp for a ceiling-raiser might be the answer.
teams.blurb: Back down to the 13th spot, Geg's team disappears at times, which makes it very difficult to win matchups. He's been unlucky with how much has been scored on him this year, but he also has the 3rd-lowest PF in the league, so the losses are deserved. If it were up to me, I'd seriously consider trading <mark class="hl-player">Kupp</mark> and getting an RB1/WR1 in return, along with a high-end flex option. This would raise Geg's ceiling while lowering his floor, but at this moment, that's what he needs to win a few weeks and get right back into the playoff hunt.

teams.synopsis: A league-high pace of season-ending injuries — the bottom of the rankings for the foreseeable future.
teams.blurb: I'm sorry, but this team will continue to be at the bottom of the rankings until he can get a more well-rounded lineup. Maney is averaging two season-ending injuries per PFFL season, which is a league high. With his RB1 and RB2 in Week 4 now out for the year, Cole will have to look to other players to step up and provide. Look for this team to try and trade for RBs, because his RB2 at the moment is <mark class="hl-player">Mark Ingram</mark>. Also, <mark class="hl-player">DHop</mark> returns soon, so watch out for <mark class="hl-player">Hollywood</mark>'s production to drop a little bit — which is the exact news Maney needs right now. There are no brighter days ahead, at least not in the next couple of weeks, but maybe this team will get back on track for the second half of the season. My advice would be to start training for the punishment, unless you get a new RB2 and/or pick up a new QB and TE (I don't know, there's so much to do with this team).
